registers.name: Vehuiah
registers.move15: 10 rises onto the toes with a sharp drop of the heels
registers.move60: Do two more sets of the rises with a one-breath pause between them, then say out loud the one action you are launching.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Take a sip of warm water and feel its temperature
registers.friction: The impulse goes into bustle: much is begun, yet no task has taken a stable form.
registers.clean: One clear step without discussion: the decision is made, the action has begun.
registers.q1: What do I want to launch right now, without waiting for permission?
registers.q2: What first step would take less than five minutes?
registers.thought: Action begins from complete silence. Do not hurry; let the impulse show itself.

registers.name: Jeliel
registers.move15: Raise your arms on the inhale, a soft forward bend on the exhale
registers.move60: Repeat the arm raise and bend six times in the rhythm of your breath, then write down two conflicting wishes, one phrase each.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Before eating, pause for 30 seconds: notice the smell and color of the food
registers.friction: Extremes: now overload, now a full stop; inner contradictions eat up your strength.
registers.clean: Two opposite wishes sit side by side, and between them there is a calm choice.
registers.q1: Which two wishes are pulling me in different directions right now?
registers.q2: What would bring back balance without a fight?
registers.thought: Strength is not in pressure but in the precision of the inner center.

registers.name: Sitael
registers.move15: Press your palms against each other in front of your chest (5 sec)
registers.move60: Press your palms together three times for five seconds, and after each time name one fact you can rely on.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Choose food with protein and healthy fats instead of fast carbohydrates
registers.friction: Doubts delay the start: support is sought outside instead of being built from what already exists.
registers.clean: You rely on what is done and on simple facts, not on certainty of the result.
registers.q1: What do I already have in order to begin?
registers.q2: Which doubt can be tested by action rather than by thought?
registers.thought: The foundation is laid before the form appears.

registers.name: Elemiah
registers.essence: Clearing away bustle, dropping mental noise
registers.move15: Vigorously shake out your hands (10 sec)
registers.move60: Shake out your hands, then your shoulders and legs for ten seconds each, and finish with a still pause of one breath.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Chew each bite slowly, about 20 times
registers.friction: A background of small thoughts and notifications: attention is split while the important stays unattended.
registers.clean: The head is quieter, one task remains, and it is visible as a whole.
registers.q1: Which single thought takes up the most room?
registers.q2: What part of the noise can I simply switch off?
registers.thought: Drop other people's friction. Your vector is clean.

registers.name: Mahasiah
registers.move15: Rotate the neck and shoulder girdle along the axis
registers.move60: Do five slow shoulder rotations backward and forward, turn the neck only within a comfortable range, then formulate one correction.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Choose whole, unprocessed foods
registers.friction: A mistake turns into self-blame while the course stays the same.
registers.clean: The mistake is noticed calmly, the correction is small and precise.
registers.q1: Where did I drift from my course, and by how much?
registers.q2: What is the smallest correction that would restore the form?
registers.thought: Any mistake is just a signal to correct the course.

registers.name: Lelahel
registers.move15: Open the chest, bring the shoulder blades together
registers.move60: Bring the shoulder blades together for five seconds and release, repeat six times, then say out loud one of your strengths.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Try food with less salt
registers.friction: The resource hides: you slouch, speak more quietly and understate what you can do.
registers.clean: The chest is open, the voice even, and you show what is already done.
registers.q1: Which of my resources is staying in the shadow now?
registers.q2: What can I show, and to whom, today?
registers.thought: Light shows itself naturally when there is no clamp.

registers.name: Achaiah
registers.move15: Static plank or holding the feet in place (20 sec)
registers.move60: Hold a plank or a foot-press twice for twenty seconds with a pause in between, breathing evenly. If the plank is hard, do the foot-press.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: Before eating, wait 15 minutes and drink some water
registers.friction: Impatience pushes you to hurry a process that ripens at its own pace.
registers.clean: You hold the line without hurry and without stopping; the result builds up gradually.
registers.q1: What is ripening in me now, and how much more time does it need?
registers.q2: Where am I rushing what cannot be sped up?
registers.thought: A seed grows in the dark without extra attention.

registers.name: Cahetel
registers.move15: A deep belly inhale and a long exhale
registers.move60: Take ten belly breaths, and on each exhale mentally name what you already have.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: Add warm fiber: porridge or stewed vegetables
registers.friction: A sense of lack pushes you to take more than you need or, on the contrary, to deny yourself everything.
registers.clean: You take as much as you need and notice what is already there.
registers.q1: What do I already have in sufficient amount?
registers.q2: What do I demand of myself beyond what is needed?
registers.thought: Accept the resource without guilt or haste.

registers.name: Haziel
registers.move15: Gently stroke the neck and collar area
registers.move60: Stroke your neck and shoulders for a minute at a calm pace, and on each exhale mentally repeat "this is".
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: Choose a drink without sugar
registers.friction: You argue with what is happening: tension rests on the thought "this should not be".
registers.clean: The fact is accepted and one step is found in it that depends on you.
registers.q1: What am I arguing with, though I cannot change it?
registers.q2: What in this situation depends on me?
registers.thought: Trust in the process takes away 90% of the load.

registers.name: Aladiah
registers.move15: Stretch the fascia of the side lines of the torso
registers.move60: Slowly bend sideways on the inhale and return on the exhale, five times each side, without pain or jerks.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: Pay attention to the texture of the food: density and temperature in the mouth
registers.friction: You keep up the load on top of fatigue and put rest off until later.
registers.clean: Rest comes on time: you notice the first signs of fatigue and respond to them.
registers.q1: Which sign of fatigue am I ignoring?
registers.q2: What kind of rest do I need now: silence, movement or sleep?
registers.thought: The body knows how to recover if you do not get in its way.

registers.name: Laoviah
registers.move15: Fix your gaze on one point for 15 seconds
registers.move60: Fix your gaze on a point for thirty seconds, blinking calmly, then close your eyes for thirty seconds and write down the first thought that comes.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: Choose a portion after which you feel light
registers.friction: The inner voice is drowned out by analysis: the answer is there, but it is given no room.
registers.clean: The first calm thought turns out to be accurate, and you trust it.
registers.q1: Which answer do I already know but do not want to admit?
registers.q2: What will the first thought say before the analysis begins?
registers.thought: The answer is already there. Turn off the background noise.

registers.name: Hahaiah
registers.move15: Clench your fists on the inhale, fully release on the exhale
registers.move60: Clench your fists on the inhale and release on the exhale six times, then name in one phrase the boundary you hold today.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: Drink water after the meal, not with every bite
registers.friction: Boundaries are blurred: other people's requests and states take your place.
registers.clean: You calmly say "no" where needed and "yes" where you want to.
registers.q1: What is being imposed on me, although the choice was not mine?
registers.q2: Which boundary can I mark today?
registers.thought: Keep the borders of your field untouched.

registers.name: Iezalel
registers.move15: Micro-rotation of the pelvis and aligning the spine.
registers.move60: Standing, make ten soft pelvic circles in each direction, then lengthen the spine upward and write down what needs to be connected with what.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Go by fullness in the stomach, not by how the plate looks
registers.friction: Scattered parts stay unconnected, and control over details prevents you from seeing the whole.
registers.clean: Connections build themselves when you stop holding everything by force.
registers.q1: Which two parts of my work or life are not connected with each other?
registers.q2: What am I trying to control instead of connecting?
registers.thought: Connections build themselves when there is no bustle inside and no wish to control the form.

registers.name: Mebahel
registers.move15: Stretch upward with the whole body, spreading the fingers
registers.move60: Stretch upward on the inhale, relax on the exhale five times, then write in one phrase what you want to say directly.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Add a little healthy fat: a spoon of oil or a handful of nuts
registers.friction: Things left unsaid create friction: you avoid a direct conversation and accumulate tension.
registers.clean: A simple direct wording releases the tension at once.
registers.q1: What am I not saying outright?
registers.q2: Which direct phrase would release the tension?
registers.thought: A lie creates friction. Directness frees energy.

registers.name: Hariel
registers.move15: Lightly tap the fingertips on the sternum
registers.move60: Tap on the sternum for thirty seconds, then divide the task into three steps on a sheet.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Eat without gadgets and screens
registers.friction: Thoughts get tangled: the task seems huge because it is not broken into parts.
registers.clean: The task is broken into three steps and the first one is clear.
registers.q1: Which three steps make up my task?
registers.q2: What in my reasoning rests on an assumption rather than a fact?
registers.thought: Order outside begins with structure inside.

registers.name: Hakamiah
registers.move15: Press the feet into the floor, a light squat with a straight back
registers.move60: Do five soft half-squats with a straight back, then name one value you will not betray today.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Swallow consciously and thank the body for the resource
registers.friction: You adjust to other people's scripts and lose your own course for the sake of approval.
registers.clean: A decision is made by your own criteria and you calmly hold it.
registers.q1: Whose script am I playing now?
registers.q2: Which of my values is not up for discussion?
registers.thought: Do not betray your vector for momentary comfort.

registers.name: Lauviah
registers.move15: Soft head tilts left and right
registers.move60: Do soft head tilts, six to each side, then play a favorite sound or look at something beautiful for thirty seconds.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Check your posture while eating: shoulders open, torso upright
registers.friction: Fatigue blocks interest: everything seems heavy, even what you love.
registers.clean: Lightness appears: interest returns without effort when the tension leaves.
registers.q1: What truly interests me today?
registers.q2: What can I remove to make things lighter?
registers.thought: Joy is the natural state of a relaxed system.

registers.name: Caliel
registers.move15: 5 deep breaths with a 3-second hold
registers.move60: Take five breaths with a three-second hold; if you feel dizzy, return to normal breathing at once, then write down the choice in one line.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Eat warm food, not scalding hot
registers.friction: The choice is postponed because you want to keep all the options and lose nothing.
registers.clean: One option is chosen and the rest are let go without regret.
registers.q1: Which choice am I putting off?
registers.q2: What can I give up for the sake of the main thing?
registers.thought: Cut off the excess without regret or drama.

registers.name: Leuviah
registers.move15: Press your palms into your thighs while seated
registers.move60: Press your thighs with your palms five times for five seconds, then write down one conclusion from recent experience.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: Add something sour: lemon or berries
registers.friction: Experience passes by: events happen, but no conclusions remain from them.
registers.clean: You record the lesson in one phrase and can use it.
registers.q1: What lesson did my latest experience give me?
registers.q2: What did the body remember from it better than the head?
registers.thought: Every detail is recorded in the body. Respect its rhythm.

registers.name: Pahaliah
registers.move15: Hold your balance on one leg (10 sec)
registers.move60: Hold your balance on each leg for twenty seconds with a support nearby, then choose one simple rule for today.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: Choose a warm herbal infusion instead of strong coffee
registers.friction: Discipline turns into pressure on yourself, and then into a breakdown.
registers.clean: Order rests on a calm rhythm, not on coercion.
registers.q1: Where am I pressing on myself instead of putting things in order?
registers.q2: Which simple rule will support me today?
registers.thought: Discipline is simply the absence of chaos.

registers.name: Nelchael
registers.essence: Knowledge of structure, taming the mind
registers.move15: Bring the shoulder blades together and apart behind your back
registers.move60: Bring the shoulder blades together and apart ten times, then draw a diagram of one topic in three blocks.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: Before eating, gently stroke your belly clockwise
registers.friction: The mind jumps from topic to topic without bringing understanding to a structure.
registers.clean: The topic is laid out: parts, connections and order are visible.
registers.q1: Which topic do I need to break into parts?
registers.q2: What links its parts together?
registers.thought: Digitize the task so that it loses its fear.

registers.name: Yeiayel
registers.move15: Circular movements of the feet in the air
registers.move60: Seated, make ten circles with each foot in both directions, then cross one optional item off your tasks.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: Sit symmetrically, elbows on a support
registers.friction: Resources are spent on the superfluous, and nothing is left for the important.
registers.clean: You spend attention and strength on what brings you closer to your goal.
registers.q1: Where does my attention go to waste?
registers.q2: What can be crossed off the to-do list?
registers.thought: Keep what you have gathered; do not scatter your focus outward.

registers.name: Melahel
registers.essence: Power of plants, grounding through matter
registers.move15: A slow bend toward the feet with bent knees
registers.move60: Bend toward the feet with bent knees five times at a slow pace, then step outside or go to the window for a minute.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: Choose a simple source of protein: eggs, fish or poultry
registers.friction: You live in your head, and the simple rhythms of the body, like sleep, food and walking, get thrown off.
registers.clean: The simple body rhythms hold, and the head becomes clearer.
registers.q1: Which simple body rhythm of mine has been thrown off?
registers.q2: What would bring me back into the body for the next hour?
registers.thought: Nature does not hurry, yet it gets everything done.

registers.name: Haheuiah
registers.move15: Hug yourself by the shoulders with a deep inhale
registers.move60: Hug yourself by the shoulders and take ten slow exhales, then name five objects around you. If the anxiety is strong and does not go away, talk to someone close or a specialist.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: When you finish eating, stay in silence for 15 seconds
registers.friction: Anxiety looks for danger where there is none and swallows attention.
registers.clean: You tell a real threat from the background and bring attention back to the current step.
registers.q1: Which of my worry is about something real, and which is background?
registers.q2: What makes me safer right now?
registers.thought: You are safe. Your core is beyond the reach of outside noise.

registers.name: Nith-Haiah
registers.move15: A pause in movement: complete stillness for 15 seconds
registers.move60: Freeze for thirty seconds, then for another thirty, watching the breath, and write down what became clear.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Drink a glass of water 20 minutes before eating
registers.friction: You fill pauses with action because silence seems like lost time.
registers.clean: A pause is seen as part of the work, and after it the decision is clearer.
registers.q1: What am I running from into busyness?
registers.q2: What will silence say if it is not disturbed?
registers.thought: True action is born in silence.

registers.name: Haaiah
registers.move15: Stroke your arms from the hand to the shoulder
registers.move60: Run your palm along each arm from the hand to the shoulder five times, then tidy up one surface.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Choose a portion of complex carbohydrates that gives even energy
registers.friction: Disorder around and inside grows while small acts of order are put off.
registers.clean: Order is kept by small regular actions.
registers.q1: Which disorder bothers me most?
registers.q2: Which surface needs order right now?
registers.thought: When forms are ordered, energy flows freely.

registers.name: Yerathel
registers.essence: Widening the boundary, stepping out of the frame
registers.move15: Press the feet into the ground ("Rooting")
registers.move60: Press your feet into the floor and shift your weight for five breaths, then name one new action you will try this week.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Relax your jaw before eating
registers.friction: The familiar frame seems the only possible one, and anything new is rejected in advance.
registers.clean: You try something new while leaning on the familiar and do not lose stability.
registers.q1: Which frame has become too tight for me?
registers.q2: What small step beyond it is possible?
registers.thought: Your support lies in the density of your own presence.

registers.name: Seheiah
registers.move15: Smooth pelvic circles with relaxed arms
registers.move60: Smoothly circle the pelvis ten times in each direction, then cross one optional item off your near-term plans.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Eat slowly, as a way of switching attention
registers.friction: You spend strength faster than it returns and do not notice the first signals.
registers.clean: The load matches your reserve of strength, and pauses appear on time.
registers.q1: What in me is going into maintaining the unnecessary?
registers.q2: Where is a pause needed before it becomes forced?
registers.thought: A pause taken in time saves you from a system failure.

registers.name: Reiyel
registers.move15: Brisk marching in place with high knees
registers.move60: March in place for thirty seconds, catch your breath, then name the habit that switched on today. If the dependence is serious, that is a reason to turn to a specialist.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Eat sitting down, not on the go
registers.friction: A habitual action switches on automatically and takes control of the choice.
registers.clean: A pause appears between impulse and action, and the choice stays yours.
registers.q1: Which automatic action do I want to notice?
registers.q2: What am I doing instead of feeling?
registers.thought: You are free of outside hooks if your center is fixed.

registers.name: Omael
registers.move15: Slow circular movements of the wrists
registers.move60: Make circular movements of the wrists for thirty seconds in each direction, then write down one small daily action for a long-term task.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Combine protein with greens
registers.friction: You check the result too early and devalue what is only growing.
registers.clean: You invest regularly and do not demand an immediate result.
registers.q1: What in my life is growing slowly?
registers.q2: Which small action can I repeat every day?
registers.thought: Give the form time to ripen. Do not pull the system by its roots.

registers.name: Lecabel
registers.move15: Fixing posture: lengthen the crown of the head upward
registers.move60: Lengthen the crown upward and hold your posture for thirty seconds, then complete one task fully, from start to finish.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: After eating take three calm inhales and exhales
registers.friction: Carelessness in small things accumulates and gets in the way of the big task.
registers.clean: You do one thing at a time and finish it neatly.
registers.q1: Which small thing needs care?
registers.q2: What am I doing by halves?
registers.thought: Precision matters. A small precise action replaces tons of bustle.

registers.name: Vasariah
registers.move15: Even out your body weight on both feet
registers.move60: Distribute your weight evenly on both feet for five breaths, then assess one situation by the facts, without emotion.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: While eating choose warm or room-temperature drinks
registers.friction: The assessment shifts: you are strict with yourself and soft with others, or the reverse.
registers.clean: The assessment rests on facts and is equally fair to you and to others.
registers.q1: Where are my assessments biased?
registers.q2: Which facts am I missing?
registers.thought: Be honest with yourself. Judge the fact, not the emotion.

registers.name: Yehuiah
registers.move15: Press with the thumb into the center of the opposite palm
registers.move60: Press the thumb into the center of the palm for five seconds on each side, then write down five tasks and number them by priority.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: Concentrate on the taste of the food
registers.friction: Chaos grows while you try to hold everything in your head.
registers.clean: Everything is written down, sorted by priority, and the first item is named.
registers.q1: What am I holding in my head instead of writing it down?
registers.q2: Which task comes first?
registers.thought: Chaos retreats before the firmness of intention.

registers.name: Lehahiah
registers.move15: A bow with a straight back
registers.move60: Do five bows with a straight back at a slow pace, then name one rule you will keep today.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: Go easy on spices: feel the pure taste
registers.friction: Your rules and your actions diverge, and inner conflict grows.
registers.clean: Action and value match, and this brings calm.
registers.q1: Where do my actions diverge from my rules?
registers.q2: Which rule will I keep today?
registers.thought: Serve your inner principle, not other people's expectations.

registers.name: Chavakiah
registers.essence: Reconciling with the past, dropping resentment
registers.move15: Soft backward rotation of the shoulder joints
registers.move60: Rotate the shoulders backward ten times, then write in one phrase what this story taught you. If the resentment is too heavy, a talk with someone close or a specialist will help.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: Do not wash down dry food with a lot of water
registers.friction: Resentment returns again and again and takes attention away from the present.
registers.clean: The past stays the past, and the lesson from it is written down.
registers.q1: Which resentment do I return to most often?
registers.q2: What did this story show me?
registers.thought: Let go of the past. It no longer has density.

registers.name: Menadel
registers.move15: Shake out one leg after the other
registers.move60: Shake out each leg for twenty seconds, then write down one task that can be simplified or handed over.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: Ask yourself: is it hunger or emotion?
registers.friction: Work takes up more room than needed and turns into a burden.
registers.clean: The load is proportionate, and rest and pleasure find their place.
registers.q1: Which task has become too heavy?
registers.q2: What can be simplified or handed over?
registers.thought: Remove the extra effort. Real action happens easily.

registers.name: Aniel
registers.move15: Isometric squeeze, a sharp release of tension
registers.move60: Clench your fists or press your elbows to your torso for five seconds, release sharply, repeat five times, then write down one unusual solution.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Choose whole food instead of flour and refined products
registers.friction: The thought goes in circles: the same arguments give no new result.
registers.clean: A fresh angle appears when the tension leaves.
registers.q1: Where am I stuck and which argument do I repeat?
registers.q2: Which non-standard option have I not tried yet?
registers.thought: Compression gives a breakthrough. Hold the focus.

registers.name: Haamiah
registers.move15: Breathing with a lengthened exhale
registers.move60: Take ten breaths with the exhale twice as long as the inhale, then mentally draw a boundary around yourself.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Drink water in small portions, not in gulps
registers.friction: Other people's emotions seep inside, and you react to what does not concern you.
registers.clean: You hear the other person and stay in your own state.
registers.q1: Whose state am I carrying now?
registers.q2: What in this situation belongs to me?
registers.thought: Your protective contour is impenetrable.

registers.name: Rehael
registers.move15: Soft pelvic rotations
registers.move60: Make five soft pelvic circles in each direction and note where tension remains in the body.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: When hurried or tense, reduce the portion and eat more slowly
registers.friction: Bodily tension stays in the same places and returns when the thought comes to an anxious topic.
registers.clean: The body is mobile, and thinking about the topic does not cause tightening.
registers.q1: Where in the body do I feel tension when I think about this?
registers.q2: Which movement softens it?
registers.thought: The fascia lets go of an old block.

registers.name: Ieiazel
registers.move15: Concentrating warmth in the center of the palms
registers.move60: Rub your palms for thirty seconds and place them on your face or chest for thirty seconds. If fatigue does not pass for weeks, it is worth turning to a specialist.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Warm food: soup or stewed vegetables
registers.friction: You demand your former pace of yourself although the resource is not enough.
registers.clean: The pace is lowered, and you restore your strength in small steps.
registers.q1: What pace is within my strength now?
registers.q2: What gives me even a little strength?
registers.thought: The warmth of the palms brings energy back.

registers.name: Hahahel
registers.move15: Aligning the right and left sides
registers.move60: Stand evenly, distribute your weight and make three side bends in each direction, then write down what is active now and what should rest.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Add fresh greens to the dish
registers.friction: You live in jerks: activity to the limit, then a complete drop.
registers.clean: Activity and rest alternate smoothly, and you notice the transition.
registers.q1: Where do I overdo activity?
registers.q2: Where is rest needed?
registers.thought: Left and right merge into a single axis.

registers.name: Mikael
registers.move15: Relaxing the jaw and neck
registers.move60: Relax the jaw, gently rock the neck forward and back five times, then put the inner argument into words.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Chew dense protein food thoroughly
registers.friction: Unnoticed tension in the jaw and neck reveals an inner argument.
registers.clean: The jaw is relaxed, the inner argument is named, and a decision is found.
registers.q1: What am I arguing with myself about?
registers.q2: Which decision would end this argument?
registers.thought: The neck is free. The head is clear.

registers.name: Veuliah
registers.move15: Rhythmic breathing in time with your own pulse
registers.move60: Put your fingers on your pulse and breathe in time with it for thirty seconds, then write down when you tend to have more strength.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: Eat without hurry, at your usual time
registers.friction: Your pace diverges from your natural rhythm: you take on tasks when you have no strength.
registers.clean: You notice your ups and downs and arrange tasks accordingly.
registers.q1: When do I usually have more strength?
registers.q2: Which task can be moved to fit my rhythm?
registers.thought: Your pulse matches the rhythm of the system.

registers.name: Yelahiah
registers.move15: Fix your gaze on one point for 15 seconds, blinking calmly
registers.move60: Look at a point for thirty seconds, then work on one task for forty seconds without switching.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: Eat without being distracted by a screen or reading
registers.friction: Attention is split among several screens and tasks.
registers.clean: Attention stays on one task until a natural pause.
registers.q1: What distracts me most often?
registers.q2: Which task is the main one now?
registers.thought: One point. One gaze. Pure light.

registers.name: Sealiah
registers.move15: Instant posture activation (lengthening the crown)
registers.move60: Lengthen the crown, open the shoulders and hold for thirty seconds, then begin the task with the simplest step.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: Choose foods with magnesium and potassium: nuts, bananas, greens
registers.friction: The resource is there but does not switch on: motivation waits for the perfect moment.
registers.clean: You switch on with a small action, and energy comes along the way.
registers.q1: What am I putting off until a suitable moment?
registers.q2: What is the simplest first step?
registers.thought: Stretching upward without a single effort.

registers.name: Ariel
registers.move15: Work on the fine motor skills of the fingers
registers.move60: Touch the thumb to each finger back and forth for thirty seconds, then check one important number or deadline.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: Tidy up the table before eating
registers.friction: Details slip away: small mistakes in numbers and deadlines eat up the result.
registers.clean: Small things are in place, objects in order, numbers checked.
registers.q1: Which detail needs checking?
registers.q2: What of mine is lying in the wrong place?
registers.thought: Precision in every millimeter of the body.

registers.name: Asaliah
registers.move15: Write down the key thought without deliberating
registers.move60: Write the key thought in thirty seconds without editing, then write one action for today beside it.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: If you ate more than you wanted, note it without self-blame and drink water
registers.friction: Insights come and vanish without turning into action.
registers.clean: The insight is written down and turned into one step.
registers.q1: Which thought came recently and vanished?
registers.q2: Which action follows from it?
registers.thought: The insight has come. The system is stable.

registers.name: Mihael
registers.essence: Calm in the midst of chaos
registers.move15: A deep diaphragmatic inhale with the center held
registers.move60: Take ten diaphragmatic breaths, mentally fix the center of the belly on the exhale, then choose one task you will do calmly.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: After eating breathe evenly, without sudden movements
registers.friction: Outer bustle pulls you in, and you react faster than you think.
registers.clean: You stay at the center while it is noisy around, and you answer calmly.
registers.q1: What knocks me off center now?
registers.q2: What can I do calmly in spite of the noise?
registers.thought: In the middle of the storm you are the still point.

registers.name: Vehuel
registers.move15: Opening the chest
registers.move60: Spread your arms to the sides on the inhale five times, then write down a big goal and three stages.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Choose light food without heavy sauces
registers.friction: The task seems unmanageable because it is not broken down by scale.
registers.clean: The whole, the stages and the next step are visible.
registers.q1: Which of my goals needs scale?
registers.q2: What is the next stage?
registers.thought: The chest is open to space.

registers.name: Daniel
registers.move15: Symmetrical distribution of body weight onto both feet
registers.move60: Stand evenly, distribute your weight equally for five breaths, then write down two arguments for and two against.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Give the body time to digest; do not rush the next meal
registers.friction: A decision is made under pressure, and later you challenge it yourself.
registers.clean: The decision is weighed, and you can explain it to someone else.
registers.q1: Which decision is worth weighing again?
registers.q2: Which arguments did I not take into account?
registers.thought: The weight is distributed perfectly evenly.

registers.name: Hahasiah
registers.move15: Scan the body with your attention from top to bottom
registers.move60: Move your attention over the body from top to bottom in forty seconds, then draw a short chain of cause and effect.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: If it is hard, choose warm soft food instead of raw and coarse
registers.friction: Effects are taken for causes, and effort goes in the wrong direction.
registers.clean: The chain is visible: what caused it, what follows and where you can intervene.
registers.q1: What actually caused this situation?
registers.q2: At which link of the chain can I change something?
registers.thought: Scan the body. No clamps remain.

registers.name: Imamiah
registers.move15: Smooth wave-like movements of the spine
registers.move60: Make ten smooth waves with the spine (cat and cow), then write down two ways around the obstacle.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: A warm herbal infusion instead of a snack
registers.friction: You push against an obstacle instead of finding a way around it.
registers.clean: You change the form of the action without losing the goal.
registers.q1: Where am I pushing instead of going around?
registers.q2: What gentle path do I have?
registers.thought: The fluidity of water inside your structure.

registers.name: Nanael
registers.move15: A steady support on the heels
registers.move60: Press your heels into the floor for five breaths, then write down three rules from your experience for another person.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Take a break from sugar and caffeine for a few hours
registers.friction: The experience stays with you because it is not shaped so that it can be passed on.
registers.clean: The experience is formulated simply, and another person can use it.
registers.q1: Which of my experience may be useful to others?
registers.q2: How can I explain it in simple words?
registers.thought: The heels are heavy. The mind is empty.

registers.name: Nithael
registers.move15: Fixing the result, releasing the palms
registers.move60: Bring your palms together and release them five times as a gesture of closing, then write down the result of the task and one thing you let go of.
registers.breath: a short inhale through the nose and a long exhale through the mouth, five cycles
registers.food: Close the meal in your mind: thank the food and stop
registers.friction: Tasks stay unfinished and pull attention back.
registers.clean: The cycle is closed: the result is recorded, the remainder let go.
registers.q1: Which task is long overdue to be closed?
registers.q2: What am I letting go of along with it?
registers.thought: The cycle is closed. The result is fixed.

registers.name: Mebahiah
registers.move15: A firm fist squeeze holding the focus
registers.move60: Clench a fist for five seconds, release, repeat five times, then write the essence of the idea in one phrase.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: Choose light protein: fish, seafood or eggs
registers.friction: The project faces criticism and other people's edits, and you lose the original idea.
registers.clean: The idea is protected: you accept what is useful and decline the rest.
registers.q1: What is the main idea of my project?
registers.q2: Which edit can I accept, and which should I decline?
registers.thought: The borders of your body are strong and clear.

registers.name: Poyel
registers.move15: Relaxing the abdominal muscles
registers.move60: Relax the abdominal muscles and take ten calm breaths, then drink some water and write down one habit that supports your strength.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: After eating relax the abdominal muscles and exhale
registers.friction: Tone is held up by caffeine and haste, not by rhythm.
registers.clean: The tone is even: simple habits support your strength.
registers.q1: What gives me an even tone?
registers.q2: What undermines it?
registers.thought: The belly is relaxed. The breath comes from the depth.

registers.name: Nemamiah
registers.move15: Straightening the neck
registers.move60: Stretch the neck upward on the inhale five times, then write a three-month goal and the nearest step.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: Try food without added salt
registers.friction: You act according to circumstances and do not see where the steps lead.
registers.clean: The goal, the stages and the nearest step are visible.
registers.q1: Where are my current steps leading me?
registers.q2: Which step would bring me closer to the goal?
registers.thought: The strategy is clear. The shoulders are down.

registers.name: Yeialel
registers.move15: Grounding by pressing the feet into the floor
registers.move60: Press your feet into the floor for ten breaths, then name one difficulty you are coping with.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: Eat slowly and savor the portion
registers.friction: The pressure seems stronger than it is, and you lose your footing.
registers.clean: You hold the decision under pressure and do not spend strength on justifying yourself.
registers.q1: What pressure am I handling better than I think?
registers.q2: What gives me support?
registers.thought: The earth holds you securely.

registers.name: Harahel
registers.move15: A structured short inhale and exhale
registers.move60: Take ten short inhale-exhales, then shape one topic into a list of three points.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: Drink in small sips, not in one gulp
registers.friction: Knowledge lies about in chaos, and finding what you need is not immediate.
registers.clean: Knowledge is written down in a structure, and you find what you need quickly.
registers.q1: Which of my knowledge is not written down?
registers.q2: Where is its place in the overall structure?
registers.thought: Digitize the silence. Keep it.

registers.name: Mitzrael
registers.move15: Releasing tension from the shoulder girdle
registers.move60: Raise the shoulders on the inhale and drop them on the exhale ten times, then write the fear in one phrase and one step toward it. If the fear paralyzes you, turn to someone close or a specialist.
registers.breath: inhale into the belly for three counts, pause for two, exhale for four, five cycles
registers.food: If you want to "eat away" anxiety, first take three slow exhales and drink a warm infusion
registers.friction: Fear drives decisions, and the shoulders rise to the ears.
registers.clean: The fear is named and stops steering: the decision is made on facts.
registers.q1: What am I really afraid of?
registers.q2: What small step toward it is possible?
registers.thought: Fear leaves with every exhale.

registers.name: Umabel
registers.move15: Slow harmonious breathing
registers.move60: Breathe slowly and evenly for forty seconds, then name what you can give to the group.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Warm broth or a clear vegetable soup
registers.friction: In a group you either dissolve or withdraw.
registers.clean: You hear others and keep your own voice.
registers.q1: In whose company do I become myself?
registers.q2: What can I give to the group?
registers.thought: Resonance found. You are in the flow.

registers.name: Iah-hel
registers.move15: Complete stop of all movement for 15 seconds
registers.move60: Freeze for a minute, watching the breath without interfering.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Drink water in silence, feeling its warmth
registers.friction: Constant movement prevents you from hearing the main thing.
registers.clean: Silence comes, and thoughts settle in it.
registers.q1: What do I hear when the noise dies down?
registers.q2: What remains when I do nothing?
registers.thought: Fifteen seconds of absolute silence.

registers.name: Anauel
registers.move15: Concentrate on the point below the navel (hara)
registers.move60: Put your palm on the area below the navel and breathe for thirty seconds, then remove three unnecessary objects from your workplace.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Put your palm on your belly and feel the warmth after a warm drink
registers.friction: The space around is overloaded and distracting.
registers.clean: The space is organized for one task, and this helps you concentrate.
registers.q1: What in my space distracts me?
registers.q2: What can be removed right now?
registers.thought: The energy is gathered in the lower point.

registers.name: Mehiel
registers.move15: Lightly tap your fingertips
registers.move60: Tap your fingertips on the palm for thirty seconds, then unsubscribe from one unneeded source or turn off one notification.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Rinse your mouth with clean water
registers.friction: Information clutter fills attention, and the important drowns.
registers.clean: The incoming flow is filtered: what is needed remains.
registers.q1: Which source of information do I not need?
registers.q2: What can I switch off today?
registers.thought: The information noise is switched off.

registers.name: Damabiah
registers.move15: A drinking pause, conscious swallowing
registers.move60: Drink a glass of water in slow sips, then put water in a visible place for the next few hours. With special medical conditions, follow your doctor's advice.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Drink water consciously, exactly as much as the body asks for
registers.friction: You forget about water until fatigue and dryness appear.
registers.clean: Water is drunk regularly in small portions, without reminders.
registers.q1: How much water do I drink without a reminder?
registers.q2: What would help me drink more regularly?
registers.thought: Water cleanses your inner contour.

registers.name: Manakel
registers.move15: Contact of the feet with the surface
registers.move60: Press your feet to the floor and say out loud five things you see and four you hear. If the anxiety is strong and does not go away, turn to someone close or a specialist.
registers.breath: an even inhale and exhale for four counts, five cycles
registers.food: Notice the lightness in the stomach and do not add food out of habit
registers.friction: Attention drifts into an imagined future and takes calm away with it.
registers.clean: Attention is in the present, and the anxiety loses its object.
registers.q1: Which future am I worrying about right now?
registers.q2: What is actually around me right now?
registers.thought: Anxiety dissolved in silence.

registers.name: Ayael
registers.move15: A deep yawn or relaxing the jaw
registers.move60: Relax the jaw and yawn two or three times, then write what useful thing a hard episode gave you.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: Relax the root of the tongue and the jaw before the next swallow
registers.friction: Hard experience remains an emotional burden without conclusions.
registers.clean: The experience is processed: you see what it gave you.
registers.q1: Which hard experience do I still need to make sense of?
registers.q2: What do I know better now?
registers.thought: The jaw is relaxed. The experience is accepted.

registers.name: Habuhiah
registers.move15: Directing warmth to the area of discomfort
registers.move60: Put a warm palm on the place of tension and breathe slowly for forty seconds. If the pain is sharp or does not pass, see a doctor.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: Give the body simple warm food and do not rush it
registers.friction: Discomfort is ignored until it gets stronger.
registers.clean: You notice discomfort in time and give yourself time to rest.
registers.q1: Which discomfort am I ignoring?
registers.q2: What would rest give me?
registers.thought: Every cell restores its form.

registers.name: Rochel
registers.move15: A slow exhale through a slightly open mouth
registers.move60: Take ten slow exhales through a slightly open mouth, then name one task for which you will restore your strength.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: Exhale slowly when you finish eating
registers.friction: Energy goes into trifles and other people's affairs.
registers.clean: You bring your attention back to yourself and spend your strength on what matters.
registers.q1: Where is my energy going?
registers.q2: What can I take back for myself?
registers.thought: The energy has returned to the source.

registers.name: Jabamiah
registers.move15: Shake out your hands
registers.move60: Shake out your hands, then your whole arms for twenty seconds each, then write down one old pattern and one new option.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: Pause the meal and let digestion rest
registers.friction: You repeat the old script while expecting a new result.
registers.clean: A new move appears: you try differently and look at the result.
registers.q1: Which old script am I repeating?
registers.q2: What can I try differently?
registers.thought: The system reboot is complete.

registers.name: Haiaiel
registers.move15: Hug yourself or put palms on the lower ribs
registers.move60: Put your palms on the lower ribs and breathe so that they move gently, for forty seconds, then name what makes you safer.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: Put your palms on the lower ribs and feel the stability
registers.friction: There is no sense of safety inside, and you stay on guard for no reason.
registers.clean: There is a sense of support: you are safe and can relax.
registers.q1: What gives me a sense of safety?
registers.q2: Where do I tense up for no reason?
registers.thought: You are inside a safe perimeter.

registers.name: Mumiah
registers.move15: Complete release of control over the body
registers.move60: Lie down or sit comfortably, relax the body part by part from the face to the feet over a minute, then write down one thought you are leaving for later.
registers.breath: an exhale twice as long as the inhale, five cycles, without effort
registers.food: Let go of control over food: eat when hungry, stop when full
registers.friction: You cannot let go of your tasks: thoughts return to them and to conversations.
registers.clean: You let go of what has been lived and allow the body to relax completely.
registers.q1: What can be let go of now?
registers.q2: What remains unclosed?
registers.thought: Food without food. Light without form. Sleep.
